concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Quadratic equations and discriminant
concepts.description: A quadratic equation has the form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0. Its discriminant is D = b^2 - 4ac. For real coefficients, D > 0 gives two distinct real roots, D = 0 gives equal real roots, and D < 0 gives a complex-conjugate pair.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Arithmetic progressions
concepts.description: An arithmetic progression (AP) is a sequence with a constant difference d between consecutive terms. Its nth term is a_n = a + (n - 1)d. The sum of the first n terms is S_n = n/2[2a + (n - 1)d], or n/2(a + l) when the last term l is known.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Trigonometric identities and values
concepts.description: Trigonometric functions describe ratios and periodic relationships associated with angles. The identity sin^2 θ + cos^2 θ = 1 holds for every real angle. When a ratio is known, this identity can determine another squared ratio, but the sign of a function also depends on the angle's quadrant.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: General term in a binomial expansion
concepts.description: For a non-negative integer n, (a + b)^n expands into terms whose coefficients are binomial coefficients. The general term is T_(r+1) = C(n,r)a^(n-r)b^r for r = 0,...,n. The exponent of a decreases as the exponent of b increases.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Slope and point-slope equation
concepts.description: The slope of a non-vertical line through (x₁,y₁) and (x₂,y₂) is (y₂−y₁)/(x₂−x₁). A line of slope m through (x₁,y₁) has equation y−y₁ = m(x−x₁). A vertical line has undefined slope and equation x = constant.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Sample spaces and event probability
concepts.description: For equally likely outcomes in a finite sample space, P(A) = number of outcomes in A divided by total outcomes. An event is a subset of the sample space. First define the outcomes carefully; equally likely counting does not apply if outcomes have unequal probabilities.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Union, intersection, and complement
concepts.description: The union A∪B contains elements in A or B or both; the intersection A∩B contains elements common to both. A complement depends on a stated universal set. Venn diagrams help represent overlap and avoid double-counting.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Modulus and conjugate
concepts.description: For z=a+ib, its conjugate is z̄=a−ib and modulus is |z|=√(a²+b²). The product z z̄=a²+b²=|z|² is real and non-negative. Complex conjugation reverses the sign of the imaginary part.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Base case and inductive step
concepts.description: A proof by induction has a base case and an inductive step. First establish the statement for the starting integer. Then assume it holds for an arbitrary n in the domain and prove it for n+1. This establishes the statement for all integers from the base onward.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Choosing and arranging objects
concepts.description: A permutation counts ordered selections; a combination counts selections where order does not matter. For n distinct objects chosen r at a time, nPr=n!/(n−r)! and nCr=n!/[r!(n−r)!]. The question’s meaning determines which count applies.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Circle equation and centre-radius form
concepts.description: A circle is the set of points at fixed distance r from a centre (h,k). Its standard equation is (x−h)²+(y−k)²=r². Completing squares converts many general quadratic equations into this form, when the x² and y² coefficients match and there is no xy term.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Derivative as a limit
concepts.description: The derivative at a point is the limiting rate of change: f′(a)=lim(h→0)[f(a+h)−f(a)]/h when the limit exists. Geometrically it is the tangent slope; in motion, it can represent instantaneous velocity from position.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Graphical solution of two-variable inequalities
concepts.description: A linear inequality in x and y describes a half-plane bounded by its boundary line. Use a solid boundary for ≤ or ≥ and a dashed boundary for < or >. Test a point not on the line to determine which side satisfies the inequality.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Complementary events
concepts.description: The complement A′ contains outcomes in the sample space that are not in A. Since A and A′ are disjoint and exhaustive, P(A′)=1−P(A). Complement reasoning is useful when counting “at least one” events is harder than counting “none.”

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Relations and functions
concepts.description: A relation from one set to another is a subset of their Cartesian product. A function assigns each domain element exactly one value in the codomain. Identify domain, codomain, and range carefully; the range is the set of values actually attained.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Introduction to three-dimensional coordinates
concepts.description: A point in three-dimensional space is represented by coordinates (x, y, z) relative to three mutually perpendicular axes. Coordinate planes are defined by setting one coordinate to zero, and distances between points follow from the three-dimensional distance formula.

concepts.subject: Mathematics
concepts.name: Measures of dispersion
concepts.description: Statistics describes and compares data using measures of central tendency and dispersion. Range is maximum minus minimum; mean deviation and standard deviation summarize spread around a chosen centre. The same average can describe data sets with very different variability.
